  across four miles of black water to the mainland,
  where a single window sat above the village of Carrow.
  At ten o'clock that window went dark, then lit, then
  went dark and lit again. Two flashes.

  He answered with the hand lamp. Two flashes. Then he
  went inside, wrote the weather in the log, and slept.

  He had never learned whose window it was. He had
  decided early on that finding out would spoil it.

  ---

  The letter from the Commissioners came in March, in
  the same brown envelope as every letter before it. It
  was polite and it thanked him. The Skerry light would
